https://www.dw.com/en/short-on-us-patrio.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IetU Eight batteries for US Patriot interceptor missiles are stationed across Ukraine, but President Zelenskyy is looking elsewhere for missiles Image: Jens Büttner/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Russia is increasingly relying on ballistic missiles for its attacks on Ukraine — precisely the weapons that Ukraine 's armed forces depend heavily on Western support to ward off. However, the crucial US -produced Patriot interceptor missiles are often in short supply. How urgently does Ukraine need new Patriot missiles? Extremely urgently. While Ukraine has set up a well-functioning defense network against drones , its armed forces are reaching their limits when it comes to fending off Iskander-M ballistic missiles. One of the few weapons capable of countering such missiles is, above all, the Patriot system with its PAC-3 interceptor missiles. At the beginning of August, it became evident once again how patchy Ukraine's air defense has become. During a Russian attack on August 1, Ukraine could only intercept one of 27 ballistic missiles fired. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said this was due to the fact that there were practically no more Patriot interceptor missiles left for the eight batteries stationed across Ukraine. Three days later, according to Ukraine, Russia fired another 24 ballistic missiles as well as four Zircon hypersonic missiles, of which none were intercepted. Ukraine faces Patriot missile shortage To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The French/Italian SAMP/T is considered an alternative to the Patriot system. However, Ukraine owns only a few of those, and the required Aster-30 interceptor missiles are also in short supply. In addition, the more powerful new-generation SAMP/T NG will only gradually become available. Therefore, the system is not a European short-term alternative to Patriot. At the same time, Patriot deliveries are declining. According to Zelenskyy, Ukraine received only about one-third as many anti-aircraft missiles so far this year as it did in 2025. The war in the Middle East has further exacerbated the global shortage. Unlike at the beginning of the Ukraine war, the problem today lies less with launching facilities and more with Patriot ammunition. What are the dimensions of Russia's missile capabilities? Although exact Russian figures are not publicly available, there are numerous indications that Russia is ramping up its production. Moscow has, for example, significantly increased production of Iskander-M and Kinzhal ballistic and air-launched missiles. According to current estimates, it produces around 60 to 65 Iskander-M missiles per month alone, which amounts to more than 700 per year. Reports indicate there are apparently shipments from North Korea as well. According to Ukraine, Pyongyang has supplied Russia with some 150 ballistic missiles since the end of 2023. In addition, a North Korean missile unit that has recently been deployed to Russia could be equipped with up to 120 additional missiles. Ukraine calls on allies to help with air defenses To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video According to Ukraine's Defense Ministry, Russia launched 195 ballistic missiles of various types in July alone. Only 29 of them could be intercepted. Ukraine's military intelligence service estimates that Russia is currently capable of firing up to 100 ballistic missiles per month without depleting its stocks. In contrast, US missile producer Lockheed Martin supplied only 620 modern PAC-3 MSE interceptor missiles worldwide in 2025. The company plans to increase its annual production capacity to 2,000 units, but only as part of a seven-year program. Did the US allow Ukraine to build its own Patriots? According to defense intelligence platform Army Recognition, an average of only some 133 Patriot interceptor missiles have been delivered to Ukraine per year since the start of the war. Given the intensity of Russian missile attacks this isn't much, which is why another option is gaining importance in Kyiv : domestic production. In the wake of the NATO summit in Ankara in July, the Ukrainian government presented the matter as largely settled. Zelenskyy cited a political decision by US President Donald Trump to grant Ukraine licenses for the production of Patriot interceptor missiles. As recently as July 28, it was declared after a meeting of the two leaders in Washington that both presidents had had talks about the "implementation" of this decision. Will there be a Patriot deal? Zelenskyy visited the White House in late July Image: Selenskyj/Telegram Three days later, Trump caused confusion. The US had not yet approved Ukrainian production; it had to be "careful," Trump said, with this kind of technology transfer. Nonetheless, the talks are continuing. According to information from Reuters news agency, American and Ukrainian representatives are considering, among other options, a model in which components are produced in Ukraine and missiles are initially assembled in Germany . Kyiv's participation in the production of a new, less expensive Patriot missile is also under discussion. How quickly could Ukraine build Patriot missiles on its own? Not fast enough to solve the current problem of overburdening. Outgoing Ukrainian ambassador in Washington, Olha Stefanishyna, estimated that setting up production of Patriot missiles in Ukraine was a process that could take anywhere from 12 months to five years. A modern interceptor missile has numerous highly specialized components. A shortage of seeker heads, electronics or missile motors, for example, can limit the entire production. Until a domestic production is established, Kyiv is trying to obtain Patriot missiles more quickly. To this end, other customers are to pass on their shipments to Ukraine and get replacements at a later date. What's the status of Ukraine's own developments? Ukraine is no longer working alone on a system of its own, but is trying to set up a European-Ukrainian missile defense project instead. The program is known as Freya. The core of the system will be the FP7.X interceptor missile provided by Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point. According to the company's CTO, Iryna Terekh, its architecture is based on Soviet designs for the S-300 and S-400 air defense systems. Today's missile, however, had only some 20% in common with its predecessors, Terekh said. Iryna Terekh, chief technical officer of Ukrainian arms manufacturer Fire Point, said the FP7.X interceptor missile is based on Soviet designs Image: Anna Pshemyska/DW Now involved in the project are, according to Fire Point, more than a dozen European arms manufacturers. Their goal is to develop an interceptor missile costing less than €1 million ($1.15 million), which would make it less expensive than the modern Patriot PAC-3 missiles ($5 million). However, this system will not be quickly available either. The Ukrainian side aims to have a prototype ready during the first half of 2027. This article was originally written in German. https://www.ibtimes.com/spacex-faces-its.text: SpaceX will report its first quarterly earnings as a publicly traded company on Tuesday after market close, marking a pivotal moment for Elon Musk's aerospace and artificial intelligence giant after one of the most dramatic post-IPO reversals in recent market history.The company, which debuted on Wall Street in June at $135 per share, quickly became one of the hottest stocks of the year before losing nearly half its value from its peak. Investors are now hoping the earnings report will provide evidence that SpaceX can justify its lofty valuation and reignite confidence after the stock's steep decline.Shares closed Monday at $114.53, down 15% from the initial public offering price and nearly 49% below the record high of $225 reached just days after trading began. It was climbing close to 4% on Tuesday at 11:31 a.m. ET. The selloff has erased more than $1 trillion in market value from its peak, making the company's first earnings release one of the most closely watched events of the earnings season, according to Bloomberg.Despite the sharp decline, analysts warn that the results themselves may not offer the clarity investors are seeking. Unlike mature technology companies, SpaceX remains unprofitable and continues to invest heavily in ambitious long-term projects spanning satellite internet, reusable rockets, artificial intelligence and future orbital infrastructure."There is so much that's in the future of the SpaceX story," Drew Cupps, portfolio manager and head of the 5Perspectives Growth Team at Polen Capital, told Bloomberg. "There's not a lot of here and now."Wall Street expects SpaceX to report a second quarter loss of 24 cents per share on revenue of approximately $6.8 billion. However, those forecasts have become increasingly uncertain as analysts struggle to model a company with limited public financial history.Bloomberg reported that consensus estimates for the company's quarterly loss have widened by about 18% over the past month, underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the business.Instead of focusing solely on the quarterly numbers, analysts say management's outlook may carry even greater weight. Investors are expected to closely scrutinize updates on the company's Starlink satellite network, commercial launch business and artificial intelligence initiatives, all of which are viewed as key drivers of SpaceX's long-term growth strategy.The earnings report also comes at a particularly delicate time because a major share lockup expiration is just around the corner.On Aug. 6, roughly 911.5 million shares valued at more than $100 billion will become eligible for sale as restrictions on early investors expire. Bloomberg noted that billions of additional shares are scheduled to be unlocked later this year, creating the possibility of increased selling pressure and greater stock volatility.The timing has raised concerns among market observers that additional supply could weigh on the shares regardless of the earnings results. "It's a total mess," Ken Mahoney, chief executive officer of Mahoney Asset Management, told BloombergOf the 39 analysts tracked by Bloomberg, 30 maintain buy ratings on the stock. Several have reaffirmed aggressive price targets despite the recent selloff. Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale continues to project the shares could climb to $800 over the next year, citing expectations for exponential revenue growth.Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas recently reiterated his $300 price target, arguing that the current share price effectively assigns no value to SpaceX's artificial intelligence business. Bernstein analyst Douglas Harned has also encouraged investors to focus less on quarterly fluctuations and more on management's long-term vision, particularly the company's ambitious plans involving orbital data centers.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Los Angeles’s mayor, Karen Bass, called for an independent evaluation into officer-involved deaths. Photograph: Damian Dovarganes/AP View image in fullscreen Los Angeles’s mayor, Karen Bass, called for an independent evaluation into officer-involved deaths. Photograph: Damian Dovarganes/AP Los Angeles LAPD releases footage of death of man whom police handcuffed and beat Jose Carlos Hoyoz-Munoz was arrested after a family altercation and restrained for ‘combative’ behavior Uwa Ede-Osifo Sat 29 Aug 2026 15.52 EDT Last modified on Sat 29 Aug 2026 15.54 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A cadre of Los Angeles police officers beat and restrained a handcuffed man in July, minutes before he was found dead in a jail cell, according to newly released body-cam footage . On 15 July, Jose Carlos Hoyoz-Munoz, 58, was found unconscious in his cell at the Van Nuys regional jail. At the time, the LAPD said two use-of-force incidents had occurred, without specifying the nature. In the video released on Friday, the department said three use-of-force incidents occurred. Body-cam footage showed Hoyoz-Munoz flapping what appeared to be a piece of cloth against the window in his holding cell. Several officers entered the cell and pinned him to the ground. The department described the restraint as being spurred by Hoyoz-Munoz’s “combative” behavior as they sought to fingerprint him. The officers placed him in a harnessed chair, which they used to transport him to the booking stalls, the video shows. Police used the weight of their bodies to restrain him again, citing resistance. The department said Hoyoz-Munoz also spat at officers, after which they put a spit hood over his face. Hoyoz-Munoz was escorted back to his cell. He was still handcuffed with the spit hood partly covering his face and his pants sagging down to his ankles, exposing his backside. After climbing on top of a toilet, officers again entered the cell. They moved him to the cell bed, piling on top of him as he was positioned face down. The department said officers conducted wellness checks for 20 minutes afterward, when he appeared to exhibit signs of life. Later, an officer saw that Hoyoz-Munoz was not moving. He was found unconscious and not breathing when they checked on him. Hoyoz-Munoz was arrested on 13 July, when police received a call about a suspected assault with a deadly weapon. Hoyoz-Munoz allegedly injured his mother and another relative with a knife. Upon arrival at the scene, an officer encountered Hoyoz-Munoz’s mother with a laceration on her arm. “He has lost his mind. He’s gone crazy,” she said in Spanish. Another family member had a wound on his arm. After an hours-long standoff with law enforcement, during which Swat agents deployed teargas, an agitated Hoyoz-Munoz was located in the residence, kneeling before a piano as he touched the keys and spoke of religion. Los Angeles police also released video showing the death of 33-year-old Alejandro Luis Garcia, whom officers fatally shot. Garcia had allegedly shattered car windows with a baseball bat. Los Angeles’s mayor, Karen Bass , described both videos as difficult to watch in a Friday statement. She called for an independent evaluation into officer-involved deaths concerning people experiencing a mental health crisis. “People who experience behavioral or mental health crises often do not receive the proper care they desperately need. Without it, they can deteriorate into behavior that can result in severe injury or death,” the mayor said. “We must rigorously examine whether our policies, training, tactics, supervision and accountability systems are sufficient.” Explore more on these topics Los Angeles US policing Mental health Karen Bass California West Coast news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/10/magy.text: Menü Kereső Magyar Péter: Ukrajnának konkrét lépéseket kell tennie a kárpátaljai magyarság jogainak biztosítása érdekében Belföld Pál Tamás Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Ukrajnának konkrét lépéseket kell tennie a kárpátaljai magyarság jogainak biztosítása érdekében ahhoz, hogy további uniós csatlakozási klaszterek megnyitását támogassák – mondta Magyar Péter miniszterelnök csütörtökön a Telex kérdésére Pozsonyban. A miniszterelnök a V4-es csúcstalálkozó után tartott sajtótájékoztatót, ahol a magyar–ukrán kapcsolatok alakulásáról is beszélt. Az MTI tudósítása szerint Magyar azt mondta, júniusban politikai megállapodás született a magyar és az ukrán kormány között a kárpátaljai magyarok oktatási, kulturális, nyelvi és adminisztratív jogairól, azonban a vállalt konkrét intézkedések egyelőre nem történtek meg. Hozzátette, hogy a Tisza Párt támogatta az első és a hatodik klaszter megnyitását Ukrajna uniós csatlakozási tárgyalásainál, de a további fejezetek megnyitását csak teljesítményalapú csatlakozás keretében tartják indokoltnak. A miniszterelnök példaként említette Szerbiát, amely ország 12 éve kezdte meg a csatlakozási folyamatot, mégis csak két klasztert nyitottak meg számukra a hatból. Magyar megemlítette, hogy Szerbiában közel 300 ezer magyar él, akik közül sokan dolgozni vagy tanulni járnak Magyarországra, és sokszor órákat állnak sorba a schengeni határon. Szerinte egyrészt emiatt, „másrészt őszinteségből sem fair az, hogy most mindenki követeli, hogy Ukrajna kapcsán nyissuk meg a klasztereket, miközben az első és a hatodik klaszterben sem történt előrelépés a tárgyalásokban”. Magyar Péter miniszterelnök sajtótájékoztatója Pozsonyban 2026. szeptember 10-én – Fotó: Huszti István / Telex Magyar Péter szerint igazságtalan lenne, ha Ukrajna gyorsabban haladna az uniós csatlakozásban, mint a feltételeket hosszú évek óta teljesítő tagjelöltek. „Ez egy nagyon sokéves folyamat, és egyáltalán nem biztos, hogy eredményes a vége” – mondta. A Telex azon kérdésére, hogy a közeljövőben tervez-e találkozni Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnökkel, azt válaszolta, hogy nem zár ki semmit. A miniszterelnök a sajtótájékoztatón arról is beszélt, hogy még nincs előrelépés a szlovák Beneš-dekrétumok ügyében. Azt mondta, bízik abban, hogy rövidesen lesz előrelépés Magyarország és Szlovákia között ebben a kérdésben. Korábban abban állapodott meg Robert Fico szlovák miniszterelnökkel, és most is megbeszélték, hogy ezeket a kérdéseket szakértői szinten elő kell készíteni, de ez még nem történt meg. Magyar azt mondta, bizalommal van az iránt, hogy a szlovák miniszterelnöknek is érdeke ezekre a kérdésekre megoldást találni. Hozzátette, teljesen egyértelmű, hogy addig bilaterális szinten nem tudnak előrelépni, amíg legalább a földek kártalanítás nélküli elvételében vagy a véleménynyilvánításért börtönnel fenyegetés ügyében nincs előrelépés. A miniszterelnök szerint a közép-európai országok közötti együttműködés erősítésében nagyobb potenciál rejlik, mint amennyit eddig kihasználtak ebből. Magyar kiemelte az észak-déli közlekedési kapcsolatok fejlesztését, például a Varsó–Prága–Pozsony–Budapest gyorsvasúti projektet, ami akár Bécset is érintheti, valamint az energiában, a védelmi iparban, a digitalizációban, az egészségügyben, az agráriumban és az élelmiszeriparban rejlő együttműködési lehetőségeket is megemlítette. A kormányfő szerint a V4-ek egy erős Közép-Európa bázisát jelenthetik, amelyhez később más országok, köztük Ausztria, Románia és a balkáni államok is kapcsolódhatnak. https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/.text: World Mid-East Europe Americas Asia Pacific Africa Syrian Crisis Islamophobia CIA chief's Moscow talks aimed at easing tensions: Lithuania by Deutsche Presse-Agentur - dpa VILNIUS Aug 31, 2026 - 10:42 pm GMT+3 Edited By Nurbanu Tanrıkulu Kızıl Lithuania's President Gitanas Nauseda attends a joint press conference during the Coalition of the Willing summit in Kyiv, Ukraine, Aug. 24, 2026. (EPA Photo) by Deutsche Presse-Agentur - dpa Aug 31, 2026 10:42 pm Edited By Nurbanu Tanrıkulu Kızıl Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said Monday that Washington had briefed him on CIA Director John Ratcliffe's talks in Moscow, describing the high-level visit as an effort to reduce tensions across the region. "I can say at this stage that the meeting achieved its stated objectives, and it was aimed at reducing tensions in the region," Nausėda said in Vilnius, according to Lithuanian media reports on Monday. "I very much hope that this message reached the Kremlin regime in good time." He did not provide further details, citing the agreed approach with Washington. An unannounced visit by Ratcliffe to Moscow last week sparked global speculation about the purpose of the trip and the possible content of the talks. Little was officially confirmed after the meeting. U.S. media reported, citing unnamed sources, that Ratcliffe had warned Russia during his Wednesday visit against attacking NATO allies. When asked about the reports, the Kremlin denied them and pointed the finger at the West. "We should not hide the fact that the meeting did not come about by chance and that the intention was to convey certain messages that had to be conveyed at this point in time," Nausėda said. In general, however, too much attention is being paid to the meeting, he added. While the regional security situation remains tense, it has not deteriorated dramatically recently, he said. In the Baltic states and also in Poland, there are fears that Russia, due to its problems in the war in Ukraine, could increasingly provoke NATO member states.
